chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about speaking during tawaf, reciting poetry, and laughing during the obligatory prayer or other than the obligatory prayer: is that proper? He said: There is no harm in it, and poetry—whatever of it is of the kind in which there is no harm—likewise.

key_terms.إِنْشَادِ: the recitation or chanting of composed speech, here referring to poetry
key_terms.الطَّوَافِ: the ritual circumambulation performed around the Kaʿbah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during tawaf or recite poetry and laugh in prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on speaking during tawaf, as well as reciting poetry and laughing in prayer. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام states that there is no harm in such matters in the cases described, and that permissible poetry remains permissible in that context.
